activities.title: New Material: Benchmark Contamination, N-gram Decontamination, and Quality Filters

source_resources.title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners (Appendix C: Benchmark Contamination)
source_resources.author: Tom B. Brown, Benjamin Mann, Nick Ryder, Melanie Subbiah, Jared Kaplan, et al.
source_resources.prerequisites: NLP evaluation metrics, n-gram text modeling.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Groundbreaking formal methodology for measuring benchmark data leakage via 13-gram overlap filtering and conservative dirty vs clean score reporting.
source_resources.safe_fallback: The 13-gram overlap equations, tokenization normalization rules, and clean/dirty evaluation derivations are fully provided.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Carlini et al. Quantifying Memorization Across Neural Language Models
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Measures verbatim memorization via k-shot prompting; GPT-3 Appendix C establishes benchmark n-gram contamination methodology.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Razeghi et al. Impact of Pretraining Term Frequencies on Few-Shot Numerical Reasoning
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Examines frequency bias; Brown et al. provides the direct algorithmic decontamination standard.

source_resources.relevant_timestamp: Section 4 Measuring and Preventing Memorization Of Benchmarks; Appendix C Details of Test Set Contamination Studies

source_resources.title: OpenAI Evals: Framework for Evaluating LLMs and Contamination Checks
source_resources.author: OpenAI Research
source_resources.permission_basis: Permissive open source reference under MIT license.
source_resources.prerequisites: Python, evaluation harnesses (MMLU, GSM8K), JSONL datasets.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Standardized evaluation repository specifying rigorous separation of eval prompts, canary GUID strings, and contamination test protocols.
source_resources.safe_fallback: Canary GUID matching, token set intersection, and leak detection scripts are implemented in the curriculum.

compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Widely adopted evaluation harness; OpenAI Evals provides explicit canary guidance and contamination check specifications.
Modern lightweight eval framework; OpenAI Evals illustrates standard test-set integrity guarantees.

source_resources.title: On the resemblance and containment of documents
source_resources.author: Andrei Z. Broder
source_resources.version_or_verification_date: IEEE Compression and Complexity of Sequences (Verified: 2026-10-30)
source_resources.license: IEEE Computer Society copyright / Academic linking only
source_resources.permission_basis: Academic citation and mathematical presentation of public algorithm.
source_resources.prerequisites: Jaccard similarity, hash functions, set theory.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Original description of the MinHash resemblance estimate that the lesson's minhash_signature exercise implements; the course explains the method in its own words.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Published academic paper available via IEEE and university archives.
source_resources.safe_fallback: MinHash algorithm derivation, signature matrix computation, and Jaccard estimation formulas are thoroughly explained and coded in the lesson.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Charikar Similarity Estimation Techniques from Rounding Algorithms (SimHash)
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Hamming distance-based fuzzy hashing; MinHash is the dominant standard for document Jaccard similarity in NLP.
Detects only 100% identical documents; MinHash detects near-duplicates differing by small edits or formatting.

source_resources.relevant_timestamp: Section 3 Estimating the resemblance and the containment; Section 4.1 Choosing a random permutation and a sample

source_resources.title: PyTorch Tutorial: Saving and Loading Models
source_resources.author: PyTorch Documentation Team
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful external reference under BSD open source documentation license.
source_resources.prerequisites: Python, PyTorch tensors and nn.Module basics.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Official documentation detailing state_dict serialization, optimizer state saving, and safe loading patterns.
source_resources.safe_fallback: All checkpoint serialization semantics, dictionary schema keys, and safe recovery steps are self-contained in lesson code.

compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: TensorFlow trackable checkpoint architecture; PyTorch's explicit dictionary is our target implementation standard.
Safetensors provides safe zero-copy tensor storage without pickle, compared directly when discussing pickle execution risks.

source_resources.relevant_timestamp: Saving & Loading a General Checkpoint for Inference and/or Resuming Training

source_resources.selection_rationale: Lead assignment-driven source for pretraining component practice and tests. nanoGPT remains a compact historical code-reading companion, not the current recommended training curriculum.

compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Simpler code layout, useful complementary reference for minimal PyTorch Transformer.
High-level API focus rather than building from raw tensor fundamentals.

source_resources.title: nanoGPT: train.py pretraining loop
source_resources.author: Andrej Karpathy
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful external reference under MIT open source license.
source_resources.prerequisites: Python, PyTorch, and Day 46-48 Transformer model architecture.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Compact historical code reference for the named implementation functions; CS336 spring2025 provides the lead component exercises. Do not infer top-p, atomic persistence or cloud budget enforcement from nanoGPT.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Historical implementation reference: nanoGPT README marks the repository deprecated (November 2025). Toy CPU reading/runs do not establish full GPU pretraining feasibility.
source_resources.safe_fallback: Runnable pretraining scripts and step-by-step tensor mechanics are fully self-contained in the curriculum lessons.

compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Heavy abstraction layer wrapping distributed training; nanoGPT exposes raw PyTorch loops without framework overhead.
High-performance enterprise distributed framework; unsuitable for local educational first-principles comprehension.

source_resources.title: Stanford Alpaca: An Instruction-following LLaMA Model
source_resources.author: Rohan Taori, Ishaan Gulrajani, Tianyi Zhang, Yann Dubois, Xuechen Li, Carlos Guestrin, Percy Liang, Tatsunori B. Hashimoto
source_resources.permission_basis: Open source reference under Apache 2.0 license.
source_resources.prerequisites: LLM fine-tuning concepts, Python dictionary data structures.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Pioneering instruction fine-tuning dataset schema establishing the instruction/input/output format widely used across open source LLMs.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Public GitHub repository by Stanford Center for Research on Foundation Models.
source_resources.safe_fallback: Standard Alpaca schemas and data transformation scripts are completely specified in lesson materials.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Wei et al. Finetuned Language Models are Zero-Shot Learners (FLAN)
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Pioneered academic instruction tuning across NLP benchmarks; Alpaca format provides the standardized single-turn JSON schema for consumer fine-tuning.
Commercially permissive instruction dataset; Alpaca establishes the architectural schema archetype.
